These results support the interpretation of the benchmark suite but do not replace it.

They show that the surviving-package surface on the flagship core is richer than a single route, but their support remains route-family-level: they do not justify a unique best strategy claim, and they do not displace the intrinsic route. If P_ int had failed and only a representative-selected route had survived, the natural reading would have shifted toward a lift-selected or protocol-indexed package. That is not the current evidential state. Interpreted modestly, this intrinsic-versus-representative asymmetry is closer to familiar contrasts between intrinsic state abstraction, predictive state, and selected refinement than to a claim that one universal abstraction recipe has been proved . The support layers are easier to interpret when kept in their proper place. The slice/dual analysis shows that the surviving-route picture is not exhausted by a single scalar tradeoff ordering: different slices can favor different material route families. This is informative but remains support-only and provisional. The staging–packaging defect atlas contributes explanatory route geometry; it is not a classifier and not even positively ordered in the simplest positive-versus-control way. It sharpens interpretation without entering the claim-bearing pipeline.
